sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能来到这里收听又一期节目。

sentences.en: Today, we're tackling, I would say, a very important question in our 20s and beyond.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要探讨一个我想说在20多岁及以后都非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: Am I actually in love or am I just attached?
sentences.zh: 我到底是坠入爱河了，还是仅仅产生了依恋？

sentences.en: I think we often find ourselves entangled in relationships and sometimes unable to distinguish between the intoxication of infatuation, the closeness of emotional attachment,
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们常常发现自己纠缠于各种关系中，有时无法区分痴迷的陶醉、情感依恋的亲密，

sentences.en: and, of course, identifying whether this is a love that lasts.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有识别这是否是一份能够持久的爱。

sentences.en: Particularly in our 20s, I think a lot of our relationships take on this very sensational passion, this fire, this need to rush into things headfirst without pausing to consider,
sentences.zh: 特别是在20多岁的时候，我认为我们的许多关系都带有这种非常轰动的激情、这种火花、这种头也不回地冲进去的冲动，却没有停下来思考一下，

sentences.en: do I actually even like this person?
sentences.zh: 我其实真的喜欢这个人吗？

sentences.en: Do I see them in my future?
sentences.zh: 我能看到他出现在我的未来里吗？

sentences.en: Or do I just like the companionship?
sentences.zh: 还是我只是喜欢这种陪伴？

sentences.en: Do I just like how they make me feel?
sentences.zh: 我只是喜欢他们带给我的感觉吗？

sentences.en: Knowing that distinction is so important, so you can actually make good decisions, actually choose the right people, rather than whoever is there at the time,
sentences.zh: 了解这种区别非常重要，这样你才能真正做出明智的决定，真正选择对的人，而不是随便抓一个当时在身边的人，

sentences.en: especially if you're someone like me who occasionally has to deliberately hold back, which I've gotten a lot better at in a lot of my relationships
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你像我一样，偶尔不得不刻意克制自己——我在很多关系中在这方面已经做得好多了——

sentences.en: to prevent falling head over heels after only a handful of dates.
sentences.zh: 以防止在仅有的几次约会后就不可救药地坠入爱河。

sentences.en: I know it's such a common experience, but importantly, attachment and love are very, very different.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一种非常普遍的体验，但重要的是，依恋和爱是非常非常不同的。

sentences.en: We develop our first attachments very young, almost immediately after birth with our parents or our caregivers because we instinctually need to be able
sentences.zh: 我们很小的时候就会产生最初的依恋，几乎在出生后不久就与我们的父母或照顾者建立依恋，因为我们凭本能需要能够

sentences.en: to rely on others for protection.
sentences.zh: 依靠他人来获得保护。

sentences.en: Before we have even the cognitive or the emotional capacity to love, we can form attachments.
sentences.zh: 在我们甚至还没具备去爱的认知或情感能力之前，我们就能形成依恋。

sentences.en: They're very foundational and the conditions for their creation is quite simple.
sentences.zh: 它们非常基础，其产生的条件也相当简单。

sentences.en: Proximity to the person in question, a sense of closeness and dependency.
sentences.zh: 与相关人员的邻近性、亲密感以及依赖感。

sentences.en: Love, on the other hand, is a lot more complex.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，爱要复杂得多。

sentences.en: It involves a deeper level of trust, of vulnerability, of compatibility and selflessness.
sentences.zh: 它涉及更深层次的信任、脆弱性、契合度以及无私。

sentences.en: It's not just about what we need from someone else, what security they can provide for us, but what we need in unison, what we need as a pair.
sentences.zh: 它不仅关乎我们从别人那里需要什么、他们能给我们提供什么安全感，还关乎我们共同需要什么、作为伴侣我们需要什么。

sentences.en: They feel alarmingly similar.
sentences.zh: 它们感觉起来惊人地相似。

sentences.en: I know that, especially if you've come to realize you've perhaps never been in love before and attachment or emotional closeness is all you kind of have to base that feeling on.
sentences.zh: 我知道这一点，特别是如果你开始意识到自己可能从未真正谈过恋爱，而依恋或情感上的亲密是你建立这种感觉的唯一依据。

sentences.en: But today, I really want to break down the difference.
sentences.zh: 但今天，我真的很想剖析这两者的区别。

sentences.en: We are going to look at what love and attachment do to us at a very biological, rudimentary level, what function they each uniquely serve and those cool ways to distinguish
sentences.zh: 我们将从非常生物学、最基础的层面来看待爱和依恋对我们做了什么，它们各自发挥着什么独特的功能，以及区分这两种感觉的那些酷炫方法。

sentences.en: between the two feelings.
sentences.zh: 我们还将剖析为什么我们中的一些人（包括我自己）会过快地产生依恋，探讨诸如焦虑型依恋风格、

sentences.en: We're also going to break down why some of us, myself included, get attached way too quickly, looking at things like anxious attachment styles,
sentences.zh: 情感确认和变量奖励，甚至成瘾模型，以及为什么在我们20多岁经历的那些重大生活变化期间，尽量保持单身或避免对人产生浪漫的依恋是很重要的。

sentences.en: emotional validation and variable reward, even models of addiction, as well as why it's important to try and stay single or prevent getting attached to people romantically
sentences.zh: 最后，当我们知道自己是那些非常容易产生依恋或与他人快速建立羁绊的人时，我们该如何保持这种情感距离？

sentences.en: during some of those big life changes that we go through in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我们该如何做到让爱缓缓发展，而不是把依恋混淆为更深厚的东西？

sentences.en: And finally, how do we keep that emotional distance when we know we are people who attach very quickly or bond to others very quickly?
sentences.zh: 在我们心仪的对象证明自己配得上之前，我们该如何将他们从我们生活的中心移开？

sentences.en: How do we make it so that we let love develop slowly rather than confusing our attachment for something deeper?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有一些答案要带给你，还有这种区别背后的许多迷人研究和心理学知识。

sentences.en: How can we de-center our love interests from our lives until they prove they deserve to be there?
sentences.zh: 所以我对这期节目感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Well, I have a few answers for you, along with a lot of fascinating research and psychology behind this distinction.
sentences.zh: 有太多内容要讲了。

sentences.en: So I'm really excited for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个非常普遍的难题，我认为澄清这两种体验之间的区别真的很重要。

sentences.en: There is so much to cover.
sentences.zh: 这是爱，还是我只是依恋？

sentences.en: I know it is such a common conundrum and I think it's really important that we set the record straight on the difference between these two experiences.
sentences.zh: 那么废话不多说，让我们深入探讨吧。

sentences.en: Is it love or am I just attached?
sentences.zh: 我知道我之前提过，我不清楚你们的情况怎样，但我有个巨大的倾向，就是很容易对闯入我生活的人产生依恋，

sentences.en: So without further ado, let us dive in.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是浪漫关系，还有朋友，甚至是同事之类的人。

sentences.en: I know I mentioned it before and I don't know about you, but I have a massive tendency to, I think, attach very quickly to the people that come into my life,
sentences.zh: 我非常像是那种要么全有要么全无的人，但通常这让我不禁怀疑，特别是在恋爱关系中，我究竟是真心爱着这个人，

sentences.en: not just romantic, but also with friends or even people like work colleagues.
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅习惯了他们的陪伴，或者我是被诸如痴迷、色欲或依恋的基本原则这样更肤浅的东西所驱使。

sentences.en: I'm very much like an all or nothing kind of person, but often what that leaves me wondering, particularly in relationships, is whether I am truly in love with that person
sentences.zh: 我认为辨别这两种感觉是我们情感工具箱中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: or I've just become accustomed to their companionship or I'm being driven by something more shallow like obsession or lust or the basic principles of attachment.
sentences.zh: 它们可能感觉起来一样，但对我们关系的质量却有着截然不同的影响。

sentences.en: And I think discerning those two feelings is a really important part of our emotional toolkit.
sentences.zh: 我也认为了解这种区别能让我们免受很多痛苦。

sentences.en: They may feel the same, but they have very different implications for the quality of our relationships.
sentences.zh: 我总是用“情境关系”（situationships）的例子来解释这一点。

sentences.en: I also think knowing the difference saves us from a lot of pain.
sentences.zh: 当然，“情境关系”是指那些感觉合理、亲密、浪漫或排他，但实际上并非如此的关系。

sentences.en: I always use the example of situationships to explain this.
sentences.zh: 通常其中一个人投入了感情，而另一个人则相当疏离。

sentences.en: Situationships, of course, are these relationships that feel legitimate and intimate and romantic or exclusive, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 现在，由于我是一个无可救药的浪漫主义者，我想我一直都是那个想要得到更多的人。

sentences.en: And typically one person is invested and the other person is quite distanced.
sentences.zh: 有时在那种情况下，事后我才意识到，我以为那是爱，我以为我对这个人有着深深的羁绊，

sentences.en: Now, because I am a hopeless romantic, I think I've always been that person who has wanted more.
sentences.zh: 其实只是一种非常自然的心理和生理反应，是对该关系所营造的情感环境的自然反应。

sentences.en: And sometimes in those situations, what I've realized in hindsight is that what I thought was love, what I thought was this deep bond I had to this person
sentences.zh: 当你花时间与某人做一些能创造连接感并主要释放催产素等荷尔蒙和神经递质的事情时，

sentences.en: was really just a very natural psychological and physical reaction to the emotional environment that that relationship had created.
sentences.zh: 比如约会、拥抱、依偎着睡觉以及共同的回忆，所有这些都为建立羁绊奠定了神经学基础，

sentences.en: When you spend time with someone doing things that create a sense of connection and release primarily hormones and neurotransmitters like oxytocin,
sentences.zh: 进而导致依恋的发展。

sentences.en: things like going on dates and cuddles and sleeping next to each other and shared memories, all of these things create the neurological premise for bonding,
sentences.zh: 从那里可能会发展出爱，但也可能不会，因为它并不总是能走到那个阶段。

sentences.en: which in turn causes an attachment to develop.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要解释这两种体验之间的关键区别。

sentences.en: And from that, perhaps love, but perhaps not, because it doesn't always get to that stage.
sentences.zh: 让我们从爱开始，特别是浪漫之爱。

sentences.en: So I want to explain the key differences between those two experiences.
sentences.zh: 在一段关系的发展顺序中，它通常遵循色欲、吸引，然后是爱的模式。

sentences.en: Let's start with love, particularly of the romantic sort.
sentences.zh: 当你超越了基本的身体吸引和那些冲动之后，这算是最后的阶段。

sentences.en: In the sequence of how a relationship develops, often it follows the pattern of lust, attraction, and then love.
sentences.zh: 而且你已经真正超越了表面层次去了解某人了。

sentences.en: That's kind of the final stage when you've passed basic physical appeal and those urges.
sentences.zh: 我想这之后可能是一种舒适感吧。

sentences.en: And you've really met someone beyond the surface level.
sentences.zh: 现在，爱背后的心理学真的很迷人，因为这可能是作为人类所能感受到的最强烈的情感之一，可能仅次于，甚至可能排在

sentences.en: I think maybe past that is perhaps a sense of comfortability.
sentences.zh: 悲伤和愤怒等情绪的前面。

sentences.en: Now, the psychology behind love is really fascinating because it's perhaps one of the most intense emotions we can feel as humans, probably only second or even probably first
sentences.zh: 因此很长一段时间以来，人们一直很想知道它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: compared to grief and things like anger.
sentences.zh: 为什么这种感觉究竟会驱使我们做出疯狂的事情，去创造杰作和音乐，去杀戮，去挑起战争？

sentences.en: So for a long time, people have really wanted to know how it works.
sentences.zh: 人们从几个方面对其进行了探讨。

sentences.en: Why on earth does this feeling drive us to do wild things, to create masterpieces and music, to kill, to start wars?
sentences.zh: 从生物学的角度来看，这种观点认为爱不过是一堆神经递质——血清素、多巴胺、催产素——在对我们的大脑起作用。

sentences.en: And they've approached it from a few ways.
sentences.zh: 他们还提出了社会的视角，认为爱具有进化的目的，因为它是建立社群和社会凝聚力所必需的。

sentences.en: From a biological perspective, this idea that love is no more than a bunch of neurotransmitters, serotonin, dopamine, oxytocin, that is doing things to our brain.
sentences.zh: 但我最喜欢的理论叫做爱的三角理论。

sentences.en: They've also offered a social perspective that love serves an evolutionary purpose because it's needed to build community and social cohesion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个综合的观点，关于爱是什么以及它不是什么。

sentences.en: But my favorite theory is called the triangular theory of love.
sentences.zh: 这个理论是在不久前发展起来的，其前提是浪漫的爱、真爱由三个成分组成。

sentences.en: And it's this integrated idea and what love is and what it isn't.
sentences.zh: 亲密感、激情和承诺。

sentences.en: This was developed a little while ago and the premise is that love, romantic love, true love is made up of three components.
sentences.zh: 这个三角上的每一个点都需要得到满足，才能说爱是存在的。

sentences.en: Intimacy, passion and commitment.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢其中某一样东西——我们这里特指恋爱关系——你拥有的东西就称不上是真正的爱。

sentences.en: Each point on this triangle needs to be fulfilled to say that love exists.
sentences.zh: 没有承诺，你就只有一段“情境关系”。

sentences.en: If you like one of these things and we're specifically talking about romantic relationships here, you have something that isn't quite love.
sentences.zh: 没有激情，你拥有的可能只是非常注重肉体或色欲而缺乏亲密感的东西。

sentences.en: Without the commitment, you have a situationship.
sentences.zh: 如果没有亲密感，你拥有的就是一段友谊。

sentences.en: Without the passion, you have something that might be very sexual or lustful without the intimacy.
sentences.zh: 现在，亲密感包含了依恋的感觉。

sentences.en: And without the intimacy, you have a friendship.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，它还包括了信任、安全感、脆弱性等要素，

sentences.en: Now, intimacy encompasses feelings of attachment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些感觉远远超出了简单的亲近或生物学上的羁绊。

sentences.en: But beyond that, it's also, you know, including things like trust, like security, vulnerability,
sentences.zh: 爱也遵循一些人所提出的相当典型的模式。

sentences.en: you know, sensations that go way beyond a simple closeness or biological bond.
sentences.zh: 因此，一组研究人员提出了几乎包含四个阶段的爱情模型。

sentences.en: Love also follows what some have proposed as a fairly typical pattern.
sentences.zh: 你从大约持续六个月到两年的欣快阶段开始，然后是为期一到五年的早期依恋，接着是危机阶段，在这个阶段我们可能会开始

sentences.en: So, a group of researchers have proposed almost a four-stage model to love.
sentences.zh: 疏远彼此，或者怀疑这真的是我们想要的吗？

sentences.en: You start off in the euphoric stage, which is around six months to two years, then early attachment, one to five years, followed by the crisis stage, where perhaps we begin to
sentences.zh: 在大约五到七年的时间里，这真的行得通吗？

sentences.en: drift apart or wonder whether this is really what we want.
sentences.zh: 最后是大约七年及以后的深度依恋、深度了解。

sentences.en: Is this really working out at around five to seven years?
sentences.zh: 其实从观察的角度来看，这在我的亲身经历中非常说得通，我看到许多我认识的人在

sentences.en: And finally, the deep attachment, the deep knowing around seven years and beyond.
sentences.zh: 大约五年那个时间点上，真切地观察到他们的关系要么转变到了另一个水平，要么彻底破裂。

sentences.en: I actually think from an observational standpoint, this makes a lot of sense in my own experience, seeing a lot of those people I've known who have been together around
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于什么是爱并没有共识，因为还有更具精神层面的观念，可能会称之为命运，或者会说那是与

sentences.en: that five-year point really observing how their relationships shift to another level or they fall apart entirely.
sentences.zh: 宇宙和我们的灵魂深度交织的东西。

sentences.en: You know, there is no consensus on what love is because there are more spiritual conceptions that might call it fate or they might say it's something deeply entwined
